brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A speciality green tea created by technicians at the Yangai tea farm in Huaxi, on the western edge of Guiyang.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: It was developed in 1999 and registered in 2002. In April 2004 a sample sold at a Guizhou tea auction for 488,000 yuan per jin, reported as a record for green tea, and that year it took top marks at the provincial famous tea review. Output was reported at about 8,000 kg in 2002 and 10,000 kg in 2003.
processing: High-temperature kill-green, rolling into strips, then rubbing into balls to raise the down; the top grades use mostly machines apart from the rubbing and down-raising, which keep some handwork.
harvest_season: From the opening of the garden, usually late February, to before Guyu; the rarest grade is picked three to five days before Qingming.
taste_profile: Expect what green teas usually give: fresh, vegetal and lightly sweet.
vintage_note: Three grades exist: treasure, special and first; the treasure grade amounts to only 5 to 10 kg a year.
